body:
Global crypto market cap sits at $2.89T, down 2.95% over the past 24 hours, which tells a more honest story than most individual coin moves suggest. The headline numbers on BTC and ETH look relatively benign, but the aggregate drawdown signals meaningful selling pressure underneath the surface, likely concentrated in mid- and small-cap names that aren't in today's data set. The Fear & Greed index edged down from 67 to 65, both readings sitting in Greed territory, so sentiment hasn't cracked — but the direction of travel is worth noting. Total 24-hour volume came in at $44.8B, which is not the kind of explosive print that would signal either capitulation or a breakout conviction move. This is a market grinding sideways with a slight bid under the majors and rot underneath.

BTC is trading at $85,121, up just 0.30% on the day and 0.29% over the past week — essentially flatlined across both time frames. The 1-hour move is -0.19%, so there's mild short-term softness but nothing alarming. BTC dominance at 59.1% is the real story here: money is not rotating into alts in any meaningful way, and Bitcoin is functioning as the risk-off destination within the asset class itself. Volume at $14.97B is moderate. Traders should watch whether BTC can hold above the $85,000 handle on any intraday dips, as a clean break below that level could shake out the shallow longs that accumulated during last week's drift higher. On the upside, a push with volume through $86,000 would be the first sign of renewed momentum.

ETH is at $2,695.28, up 0.49% on the day but down 0.52% on the week, which puts it in mild underperformance relative to BTC. Volume of $4.71B is respectable but not a catalyst. ETH dominance at 11.4% continues to compress relative to BTC's 59.1%, and that ratio is telling you something about where conviction lies right now. Among the notable movers, BNB was the standout at +2.25% to $788.72 on solid volume of $0.76B — the only major that looks like it had actual buying interest rather than passive drift. LINK added 1.81% to $14.11 and SOL gained 1.58% to $121.33, both outperforming ETH on the day, though both remain negative on the week at -1.20% and -2.09% respectively. On the ugly end, UNI dropped 1.32% to $9.02 and is down 9.19% over 7 days — that is a meaningful drawdown for a top-tier DeFi name and worth watching for contagion into the broader DeFi complex. ADA at $0.244893 is functionally flat on the day, down 4.66% on the week, and continuing to lose relevance in the flow conversation. DOT at $1.19 tells a similar story.

The macro and regulatory backdrop is providing a complicated backdrop. The Clarity Act stalling in Congress, per CoinDesk, removes a potential near-term catalyst for institutional product launches, though the same report notes bankers are not pulling back from crypto dealmaking — suggesting the deal pipeline is being driven by anticipated eventual clarity rather than legislative urgency. The IMF disbursing $138 million to El Salvador after granting Bitcoin waivers, per Cointelegraph, is a quietly significant data point: it validates a model where sovereign Bitcoin adoption coexists with multilateral lending, and removes a tail risk that had been overhanging that experiment. Russia's Finance Ministry paying wages in digital rubles for the first time, also per Cointelegraph, adds another data point to the slow-burn narrative of state-level CBDC adoption under sanctions pressure. Japan adding Garantex to its Russia sanctions list tightens the compliance perimeter further for any exchange with Japanese exposure. Cathie Wood's public commentary flagging AI agent spending patterns as a macro signal is directionally interesting for crypto infrastructure plays but does not move the tape today.

The near-term setup comes down to a few clear catalysts and risks. On the positive side, NEAR Intents recovering the entire $3.8 million stolen in its exploit after issuing an ultimatum to the exploiter, per Cointelegraph, is a small but genuine confidence signal for the DeFi security narrative — full recovery outcomes remain rare and deserve more credit than the market typically assigns them. Watch BTC's ability to hold $85,000 as support; any close below that level on meaningful volume changes the short-term technical picture materially. The UNI bleed at -9.19% weekly deserves a close watch — if it accelerates or spreads to other DeFi governance tokens, that would indicate sector-specific selling rather than broad market noise. The stalled Clarity Act means regulatory uncertainty remains the dominant overhang for U.S.-facing crypto businesses, and any fresh Congressional movement in either direction would be an immediate repricing event. Crypto job postings tripling to over 1,200 in September, per CoinDesk, is a lagging indicator of industry health, but falling applications suggest the talent dynamic is shifting — worth watching for what it signals about growth-phase confidence among builders.
